prs.title: fix(streamable-http): wait for post_writer before yielding
prs.author: Epochex
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: post_writer is spawned into the TaskGroup without waiting for it to actually start consuming from write_stream_reader before the caller proceeds/yields the streams. If a caller sends a message immediately after entering the streamable-http client context, it can race with post_writer's startup and be dropped or processed too early. Both PRs fix this identically: add a `task_status: TaskStatus[None] = anyio.TASK_STATUS_IGNORED` parameter to `post_writer` and call `task_status.started(None)` right after entering the stream context managers, which only takes effect if the call site also switches from `tg.start_soon(post_writer, ...)` to `tg.start(post_writer, ...)` to await that signal. (2 PRs)

members.title: Race condition in streamable http
members.author: AydarAkhmetzyanov
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2666: post_writer is spawned into the TaskGroup without waiting for it to actually start consuming from write_stream_reader before the caller proceeds/yields the streams. If a caller sends a message immediately after entering the streamable-http client context, it can race with post_writer's startup and be dropped or processed too early. Both PRs fix this identically: add a `task_status: TaskStatus[None] = anyio.TASK_STATUS_IGNORED` parameter to `post_writer` and call `task_status.started(None)` right after entering the stream context managers, which only takes effect if the call site also switches from `tg.start_soon(post_writer, ...)` to `tg.start(post_writer, ...)` to await that signal.

members.title: Race condition in streamable http
members.author: AydarAkhmetzyanov
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2666: post_writer is spawned into the TaskGroup without waiting for it to actually start consuming from write_stream_reader before the caller proceeds/yields the streams. If a caller sends a message immediately after entering the streamable-http client context, it can race with post_writer's startup and be dropped or processed too early. Both PRs fix this identically: add a `task_status: TaskStatus[None] = anyio.TASK_STATUS_IGNORED` parameter to `post_writer` and call `task_status.started(None)` right after entering the stream context managers, which only takes effect if the call site also switches from `tg.start_soon(post_writer, ...)` to `tg.start(post_writer, ...)` to await that signal.

clusters.pick_reason: #2478 fixes pickling generically at the MCPError base: it adds a _restore_mcp_error(exc_type, error) dispatcher that calls exc_type.from_error_data(error) for any subclass, with an explicit special case for UrlElicitationRequiredError (exc_type.from_error(error)) since its from_error interprets error.data as a list of elicitations. This covers every current and future MCPError subclass, not just UrlElicitationRequiredError. It also drops the `# pragma: no cover` on the `data` property, indicating that property is now exercised by the round-trip. #2555 only adds a __reduce__ override scoped to the single UrlElicitationRequiredError subclass, so it does not fix pickling for any other MCPError subclass that might hit the same TypeError. Since #2478's dispatcher already special-cases UrlElicitationRequiredError via from_error, it subsumes the fix in #2555; #2555's test additions (tests/shared/test_exceptions.py) should be ported over to #2478 before merging.
